content: {"summary":"The May 2026 outage was caused by the primary’s disk filling up with PostgreSQL WAL files that could not be archived; the backlog of WAL segments exhausted the volume, leading to ENOSPC and session termination with SQLSTATE 57P02, which broke payments‑api connections.","likely_cause":"Failed WAL archiving caused pg_wal segments to accumulate and fill the data volume.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"WAL archiving failures caused WAL segments to accumulate and fill the volume","evidence_ids":["INC-0157#0"],"quote":"segments accumulated instead of being cleared, and the volume filled from the inside"},{"text":"Sessions were dropped with SQLSTATE 57P02 when the primary ran out of space","evidence_ids":["INC-0157#0"],"quote":"Sessions that were connected at that moment were dropped with SQLSTATE `57P02`"}],"next_checks":["Examine archive command logs for failure reasons","Verify connectivity to object storage used for WAL archiving","Check alert thresholds for archiver failure counts and disk usage","Confirm emergency space reserve policies on the primary volume"]}
